newsitem.title: JORDAN: First Iraq food cargo via Jordan port in mid-April.
newsitem.headline: First Iraq food cargo via Jordan port in mid-April.

text.p: A vessel carrying 52,000 tonnes of French wheat purchased under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations will discharge at Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba in mid-month, shippers said on Monday.

The shipment, sold by supplier Glencore, is the first cargo under the deal to be shipped to Iraq through Jordan, they said. It is expected to dock at Aqaba on Wednesday 16 or Thursday 17, shippers said.
Shippers said another 50,000 tonne shipment of French wheat to Iraq from the same supplier was expected at Aqaba by the end of the month.
Aqaba has suffered since most Iraqi cargo was halted with the imposition of a U.N. embargo on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.

So far most of Baghdad's imports under the oil-for-food deal are being delivered to Um Qasr, Iraq's sole sea outlet. But Jordanian officials and shippers hope at least 20 percent of the accord's purchases will be go through Aqaba.
